jobText:
Senior Frontend Engineer — Synthetic Atlas

About Synthetic Atlas

Synthetic Atlas builds scheduling software for regional clinics. Our teams are small, our releases are frequent, and our customers tell us when something breaks. We believe in clear ownership, thoughtful code review, and leaving systems better than we found them. This posting describes a senior individual-contributor role on the patient-facing web team.

Life at Synthetic Atlas

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, twenty days of paid time off, a learning stipend, parental leave, and a home-office budget. We hold two in-person team weeks a year and otherwise work remotely across North American time zones. Our interview process is four conversations over two weeks, and we share written feedback at each stage.

Equal opportunity

Synthetic Atlas is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. If you need an accommodation during the application process, tell your recruiter and we will arrange it.

How we work

Engineers pair with designers from the first sketch, write their own tests, and own what they ship through production. We prefer boring technology and clear documentation. We hold a weekly demo and a monthly retro, and we treat incidents as learning opportunities rather than blame.

What you will do

Build and maintain the patient scheduling interface in production React and TypeScript. Keep every screen accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA. Write and maintain automated end-to-end tests. Review pull requests from four other frontend engineers. Partner with the design-system group on shared components.

What we need

Five or more years building production React and TypeScript applications. Demonstrated accessibility (WCAG) experience on shipped products. Automated end-to-end testing with Playwright or Cypress. Clear written communication.

Nice to have

Experience contributing to a shared design system. Healthcare or scheduling domain exposure.

To apply

Send a resume and a short note about a frontend system you kept accessible under deadline pressure. We read every application and reply within a week.
resumeText: Senior Frontend Engineer at Synthetic Loom. Built production React and TypeScript interfaces to WCAG accessibility standards for six years, wrote automated Playwright end-to-end tests, and reviewed pull requests for three product teams.

jobText:
Firmware Engineer — Synthetic Crestline Instruments

Our story

Synthetic Crestline Instruments has built laboratory sensors since 1998. We started in a garage with one pH probe and now ship forty instrument lines to universities and manufacturers on four continents. We remain family owned, profitable, and allergic to meetings that could have been a note. Our engineering group is thirty-two people across firmware, electrical, and mechanical disciplines.

What you will own

Firmware for a new family of battery-powered sensors: write C on an ARM Cortex-M microcontroller under FreeRTOS, implement low-power modes, bring up new boards with the electrical team, and debug with an oscilloscope and logic analyzer when the datasheet lies.

What we need

Three or more years of embedded C development. Experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar). Comfort with hardware debugging tools. Preferred: Bluetooth Low Energy stacks and unit testing on host.

What we offer

Medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with a 5% match; twenty days of paid time off plus the week between Christmas and New Year; a $2,000 annual learning budget; and a quiet lab with good coffee. Salary $110,000-$140,000 per year depending on experience.

Equal opportunity

We hire without regard to race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status, and we provide accommodations on request.
